dedupe_keys.name: public space patterns for community resilience pattern language rotterdam fieldwork

description: This dataset is a set of interconnected design patterns, a pattern language, that turns socio-spatial understanding of public space into design and planning tools for strengthening community resilience. It was published on 4TU.ResearchData on 11 June 2026 by Sahar Asadollahi asl zarkhah and Nihan Oya Memlük Çobanoğlu as the data behind the article 'Public Space Patterns for Community Resilience: From Theory to Practice', a finding of a PhD. The patterns were developed through literature review, empirical fieldwork in Rotterdam and expert validation, and address accessibility, safety, restorativeness, responsiveness, flexibility, liminality, narrativity and empowerment. Coverage: grounded in Rotterdam public spaces, intended for general use. Access: PDF from 4TU.ResearchData. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: qualitative design guidance, not measured data. Simulation uses: structuring criteria for evaluating public spaces in resilience planning and co-design. Related records: the Inclusive Public Space interviews and the Tirana Astir public space scenarios.
